title: Taiwan’s chipmaking giant TSMC to invest $1B in Anthropic, OpenAI
gist: TSMC's board approved up to $500M in OpenAI preferred stock and $500M in Anthropic common shares at its expected IPO price, adding to circular financing between AI suppliers and customers that analysts say obscures real demand. TSMC can afford it after six straight record-profit quarters (>$23B in Q3 2026), and the bet is small next to Nvidia's $30B in OpenAI and $10B in Anthropic.

insights.claim: TSMC's board approved investing up to $500 million in OpenAI preferred stock reserved for large investors and $500 million in Anthropic common shares at Anthropic's expected IPO price.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Hsu
insights.so_what: Signals an expected Anthropic IPO and gives TSMC direct upside in AI model developers.

insights.claim: The Wall Street Journal reported TSMC's investment may give markets a shot of confidence as the AI trade shows signs of strain.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Hsu
insights.so_what: Supplier endorsements may support AI sentiment during a wobble in tech stocks.
insights.quote: “a shot of confidence as the artificial-intelligence trade shows signs of strain,”

insights.claim: TSMC reported six consecutive quarters of record profit on AI chip demand, earning more than $23 billion in the July–September 2026 quarter.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Hsu
insights.so_what: Demonstrates the scale of AI-driven foundry profitability.
insights.locator: Still, TSMC has plenty of money

insights.claim: Analysts warn that circular financing among AI investors, suppliers, and customers makes it difficult to evaluate real market demand for AI hardware and services.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Hsu
insights.so_what: Circularity may inflate apparent AI demand, a key risk to AI-exposed valuations.

insights.claim: Because Anthropic and OpenAI buy huge quantities of TSMC-manufactured AI hardware, TSMC's stake fits the broader circular financing trend of the AI boom.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Hsu
insights.so_what: Vendor financing of customers can mask demand fragility.

insights.claim: Nvidia has invested $30 billion in OpenAI and $10 billion in Anthropic, plus tens of billions in other AI and robotics companies, dwarfing TSMC's $1 billion commitment.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Hsu
insights.so_what: Nvidia's exposure to its own customers' equity is far larger and more concentrated.

insights.claim: TSMC fabs produce the vast majority of Nvidia's AI data center chips and most of Apple's custom chips, with fabs mainly in Taiwan plus Japan, China, an expanding Arizona cluster, and a new fab under construction in Germany.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Hsu
insights.so_what: TSMC is a single chokepoint for AI and Apple silicon, concentrating geopolitical risk in Taiwan.
